assessments.technical_explanation: The candidate is a `new Function(...)` call inside a test file. The function body is constructed from source code extracted by brace-counting from the project's own index.js, read locally via readFileSync. No external or untrusted input reaches the dynamic function constructor; the evaluated code is the project's own source. This is a common unit-testing technique for scripts that lack module exports.

observations.title: All dynamic-execution matches are test-harness function extraction
observations.technical_explanation: Every candidate in this file is a `new Function` call used to extract a named function from the extension source and execute it with mocked dependencies for unit testing. The file imports only fs and jsdom, uses local fixtures, and mocks fetch and settings. There is no production execution, credential access, or external network data flow.
observations.layman_explanation: All flagged code is part of a test file that pulls functions out of the extension to test them in isolation. None of it runs in the actual extension or touches real user data.
